svg.title: Container isolation topology
svg.desc: A container started with network none holds the provider binary and up to two loopback bridges. Each bridge frames its traffic over a docker exec -i pipe to HostGateway, which pins one upstream, injects the host-held credential and enforces the authority's MCP tool allowlist before the host MCP handler runs.

g.text: Hover a box for its role and the fact that bounds it; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: DEPLOYMENT · one container per Container Authority
The container has no network and no credential. Provider traffic and MCP calls leave it only through host-opened pipes.

g.class: e f-engine t-hard t-mounts t-bin t-pbridge t-mbridge

g.text: claude or codex · provider binary from the configured image; Claude and Codex only
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (Claude) or the generated Codex config points at the loopback bridge; the container has no socket and no network.
provider bridge · dartclaw-bridge --surface=provider --port=8080, started by the host with docker exec -i
Holds no credential and chooses no destination; it only frames traffic over its stdio. The executable is mounted read-only (dartclaw_bridge).
mcp bridge · dartclaw-bridge --surface=mcp --port=8081; started only when the authority was granted MCP tools
With no allowlisted tools the surface does not exist, so the container has no route to /mcp at all (ContainerManager.hasMcpBridge).
restricted profile: no workspace mounts, no host home
Mounts · SecurityProfile mounts plus the read-only bridge executable and per-authority generated client state
No host home is ever mounted, so provider login state stays outside the boundary; generated state is removed with the container.
Hardening · flags ContainerManager sets at create time
The owner label dartclaw.data-dir=<dataDir> lets a restart reclaim stray containers; a container never outlives its authority.
principal comes from the pipe, never a frame
HostGateway · registers a GatewayAuthority per container; the pipe a request arrives on fixes its principal, upstream, credential, tools
A bridge process that exits or is killed revokes its surface for good, so a captured pipe or request id cannot be revived by a later execution.
Host-held credentials · SubscriptionCredentialStore and the named credential store, read per request through the provider adapter
A credential that turns unusable mid-turn raises one operator alert and releases the authority, which destroys its container.
/mcp tool dispatch, scoped to the authority
allowlist, guards and audit run before the tool
McpProtocolHandler · the /mcp handler scoped to one authority: deny-by-default canonical tool allowlist, POST only, 1 MiB request cap
Caller policy, guard evaluation and audit run before the tool, as for any /mcp caller.
creates, starts and destroys the container
reclaims strays by data-dir label at startup
ContainerManager · one per authority: docker create (or run), start, exec, stop and rm, on docker or podman
Single-use: a lost container is never recreated; the execution acquires a new authority. Name: dartclaw-<fnv1a32(dataDir)>-<profile>-<authority>.
docker or podman · the host container runtime, detected at startup; its engine architecture decides which bridge variant runs
Container isolation is unavailable on native Windows; container.enabled: true there is startup-fatal.
Provider API · exactly one upstream pinned per adapter when it is built (AnthropicMessagesAdapter, OpenAiResponsesAdapter)
A request to any other origin is refused with 403. Codex subscription mode pins chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex instead of api.openai.com.
